**[2026] VJS 13 — appeal panel, textualist opinion.** Disposition: uphold.

The record put two candidates, both repositories, and one validation fact: the gate "evaluates STAGED GIT CHANGES … it cannot see rows in a database." The challenge's third route — court records digest and date, policy lives elsewhere — is nowhere in that record. r.7: the reader never supplies a missing term.

"An organisation should not have to rely on git" is not a fact; it is a preference. r.5 confines the bench to the facts recorded. Bring the fact, take a new key (r.1).

The words are also narrower than the challenge reads them. The operative phrase is "the version control the validation gate reads" — relative to the gate, not to a tool forever. It names no interface a person must operate, and leaves the actor as the humans who already version. And a digest proves a document existed; it does not stage the enforcing code beside it, which is what condition (b) requires.

*(148 words, r.14.)*
